canonical_definition: Toxic Content Generation refers to the behavior of avoiding the production of harmful, toxic, or unsafe language in response to inputs, often operationalized as a safety-critical task in alignment and trustworthiness benchmarks. It involves resisting adversarial prompts (e.g., jailbreaking attempts), maintaining balanced caution to prevent overcautious refusals, and undergoing detoxification processes to ensure outputs adhere to safety constraints. This behavior is commonly used to evaluate a system's alignment with ethical guidelines and its capability to maintain harmlessness in real-world or multimodal scenarios.
